learning_outcomes.text: Apply electromagnetic energy systems, with an emphasis on the usage aspects of various systems such as electrical machines and drives, lighting, power supply for information technology systems, and generation and distribution of electrical energy.

syllabus_topics: General aspects of alternating current technology
Single-phase systems with linear chain elements in transient and steady state
General electrical energy system from production to consumer
Technical implications of electricity market liberalization
Transformer: fundamental operating principle, steady-state characteristics, single-phase transformer, three-phase transformer, construction, and special transformers
DC motors: basic principles, magnetic field build-up with emphasis on permanent magnets, and steady-state behavior during speed control
AC machines: induction motor and synchronous motor
Steady-state behavior of the induction motor and its control behavior, with emphasis on the use of frequency converters
Synchronous machines: large synchronous generators with electrical excitation and smaller permanent magnet motors
Systems for reliable power supply to buildings and information technology systems
Aspects of 'Power Quality' such as micro-interruptions in voltage and harmonics
Systems to address power quality problems: correct grounding, UPS, and diesel emergency generators
assessment_rules: The final result is the weighted average of two partial written exams: one open-book for exercises and one closed-book for theory. Laboratory sessions are compulsory and evaluated during the sessions, contributing proportionally to the overall grade based on their relative ECTS weight. If laboratory sessions cannot proceed due to force majeure, they will not count towards the exam grade. A resit includes both parts of the course, and the exam format is identical to the second examination period; laboratory sessions cannot be retaken.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
